topic: Dissertation Literature Review: The Synthesis Matrix

copy.instagram:
Staring at a pile of 40 papers and feeling like your lit review is just a glorified book report? You’re not alone. Most students fall into the ‘author-by-author’ trap, listing what each person said without actually connecting the dots. That’s a one-way ticket to a 2:2.

To hit a First, you need a synthesis matrix. Stop summarizing and start synthesizing. Look for the theoretical debates, compare the sampling flaws, and isolate exactly where the current research fails to answer your specific question. 

Slide through to see the difference between a descriptive summary and a critical argument. 

[Slide 1: The Trap] Don’t just list authors. 
[Slide 2: The Fix] Group by themes and gaps.

Save this for when you’re staring at your screen at 2 AM. Need a hand structuring your argument? Check the link in our bio to see how we help with lit reviews.

copy.facebook:
We’ve all been there: it’s late, you’ve got forty papers open on your laptop, and your literature review feels like a messy, disconnected list of summaries. It’s the most common hurdle for dissertation students, but it’s also the easiest to fix once you change your approach.

If you want to move from a descriptive ‘book report’ style to a First-Class critical synthesis, stop organizing by author. Start organizing by theme.

Here is the shift you need to make:
• The Trap: Summarizing individual papers one by one.
• The Fix: Grouping studies by the debates they engage in.
• The Secret: Critically comparing methodologies to highlight the 'gap' your research is filling.
